recent_post_titles: Ruby on Rails CVE-2026-66066
The word "audit" just made my coffee go cold.
Finally tested our backups.
Compliance checklist says "secure."
My LinkedIn says "CISSP."
MITRE rejected 54 fake SQLite CVEs.
Another phishing simulation, another coworker clicks the 'free iTunes gift card' link.
We backup every night, but the last time we actually tried to restore was during the fire drill and the tape was blank.
I got hit by our own phishing test todayclicked the fake password reset link and now I have to explain to SOC why Im the villain.
I have the CISSP, the CEH, and still feel like Im just Googling how to spell 'firewall' every morning.
Apple bug bounty policy floods with fake reports.
I patch, monitor, and answer phishing emails all in one coffee break.
I only test backups when the data is gone.
Marketing spends on ads, I spend on firewalls, and the CFO thinks I'm overpaying.
Audit day: I pretend my logs are clean while the auditor looks for holes.
Langflow has a critical flaw.
Spending three weeks on a SOC2 audit just to realize we're still using 'Password123' for the admin account.
The backup failed during the restoration attempt.
I'm currently the SOC, the DevOps, and the person who fixes the office printer.
I've got three CISSP certifications but I'm still terrified someone's going to ask me how a subnet mask actually works.
NatJack zero-day hits major NAT devices. Exploit actively scanning shodan.io. Patched binaries in vendor repos. Sysadmins sleeping on this are already pivoting. Silently pivoting.
Use qwerty123 for work and personal? Sure. Im a security person. No youre not.
Backups? Yeah. Tested? No. Trusted the cinematic third-act save. *Cue loading cursor.*
Marketing gets 10x my budget. Cybersecurity is a buzzword for C-suite.
Clicked the documen-t thesis phishing email. Still top performer for quarterly review.
